help.symvault:
Quick Start:
  symvault init            create a vault and identity
  symvault add <name>      add a credential
  symvault get <name>      retrieve a credential

Symaira Vault is a Go CLI password manager with an interactive TUI, multi-device
sync via Git, and an MCP server for AI-agent integration.

First-time setup:
   1. symvault init         create a vault and identity (non-interactive)
   2. symvault setup        same, plus guided wizard for sync/agents (TTY only)
   3. symvault doctor       health-check and self-heal

Daily use:
  symvault add <name>      add a credential (interactive form)
  symvault ui              browse and edit the vault in a TUI
  symvault get <name>      print a credential
  symvault --help          full command list

Usage:
  symvault [command]

Essentials:
  add              Add a new password entry
  delete           Delete a password entry
  doctor           Check vault health and configuration
  edit             Edit an existing password entry
  find             Search for entries
  get              Get a password entry
  init             Initialize a new password vault
  list             List password entries
  set              Set a password entry or field
  setup            Interactive setup wizard for Symaira Vault
  ui               Launch the interactive terminal UI

Vault:
  broker           Run the egress credential broker (loopback MITM proxy)
  dynamic          Generate dynamic secrets with time-limited leases
  file             Store, export, and consume file attachments in the vault
  generate         Generate a secure password
  recipients       Manage vault recipients for multi-user encryption
  run              Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables
  template         Generate configuration files from templates

Sharing & Sync:
  backup           Create a backup archive of the vault
  device           Manage paired devices for multi-device vault access
  export           Export vault entries to CSV or JSON
  git              Git operations on vault
  import           Import entries from another password manager
  intake           Review-gated credential intake from loose files
  remote           Manage git remote for vault sync
  restore          Restore vault from a backup archive
  share            Manage secret sharing between agents
  sync             Sync vault with remote (pull + optional push)

Agents & MCP:
  agent            Manage agent profiles
  approval         List and decide pending agent approval requests
  mcp              Start MCP server for agent access

Auth & Access:
  auth             Manage vault unlock authentication
  lock             Lock the vault (clear session)
  unlock           Unlock the vault and cache the passphrase

Administration:
  audit            View MCP audit logs
  config           Manage Symaira Vault configuration
  migrate          Vault migration commands
  policy           Manage declarative policies
  profile          Manage vault profiles
  startup-profile  Measure and report CLI startup time
  update           Check for Symaira Vault updates
  verify           Verify vault entry integrity against manifest

Additional Commands:
  completion       Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help             Help about any command
  version          Print the version of Symaira Vault

Flags:
      --color string      When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never (default "auto")
  -h, --help              help for symvault
      --json              Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified
      --no-pipe-warning   suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets
      --output string     Output format (text, json, yaml) (default "text")
      --profile string    use a named vault profile
      --quiet             suppress non-error output
      --theme string      Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)
      --vault string      path to the password vault (default "~/.symvault")

Use "symvault [command] --help" for more information about a command.
help.symvault add:
Creates a new password entry in the vault.

The entry name can use slash notation for organization (e.g., work/aws).
Interactive mode prompts for username, password, and URL.

Usage:
  symvault add <name> [flags]

Aliases:
  add, new, create

Examples:
  symvault add github
  symvault add work/aws
  symvault add personal/bank
  symvault add github-token --value "my-secret-token"
  symvault add secure-pass --generate --length 20
  symvault add aws-key --type api_key --value "AKIA..."
  symvault add ssh-key --type ssh_key --usage-hint "Production server key"

Flags:
      --allow-empty           Allow empty value for sensitive fields
      --auto-rotate           Enable automatic rotation reminder
      --expires-at string     Expiration date (RFC3339 format)
      --force                 Skip password strength validation
      --generate              Generate a secure password (non-interactive)
  -h, --help                  help for add
      --length int            Generated password length for --generate (default 20)
      --notes string          Notes (non-interactive)
      --stdin-totp-secret     Read TOTP secret from stdin (prevents argv leak)
      --stdin-value           Read password value from stdin (prevents argv leak)
      --totp-account string   TOTP account name/username
      --totp-issuer string    TOTP issuer/service name
      --totp-secret string    TOTP secret key (base32 encoded, visible in process listings)
      --type string           Secret type (api_key, bearer_token, basic_auth, ssh_key, password, certificate, database_url, totp_seed, custom). Auto-detected if not specified.
      --url string            URL (non-interactive)
      --usage-hint string     Usage hint for AI agents
      --username string       Username (non-interactive)
      --value string          Password value (non-interactive, visible in process listings)

Global Flags:

help.symvault agent install:
Unified install command that detects an AI agent, creates a security
profile in config.yaml, generates a scoped access token, injects the
MCP server configuration into the agent's config file, and installs the
embedded skill package — all in one step.

This replaces the older mcp install, mcp-config, and agent setup commands.

The default security tier is "safe" (read-only capabilities). For "standard"
or "admin" tiers, an interactive terminal is required to confirm the
security implications.

Supported agents: openclaw, claude-code, hermes, codex, opencode

Usage:
  symvault agent install [name] [flags]

Examples:
  # Install and configure Claude Code (auto-detect)
  symvault agent install claude-code

  # Detect all installed agents and configure each
  symvault agent install --auto-detect

  # HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token
  symvault agent install hermes --http

  # Standard tier with explicit confirmation
  symvault agent install codex --tier standard

  # Preview what would happen without writing anything
  symvault agent install openclaw --dry-run

  # Only install the skill package, skip MCP config
  symvault agent install opencode --skill-only

  # Only inject MCP config, skip the skill
  symvault agent install claude-code --config-only

  # Force overwrite existing profile and MCP config entries
  symvault agent install hermes --force

  # Structured JSON output for scripting
  symvault agent install opencode --output json

Flags:
      --auto-detect   Detect all installed agents and configure each
      --config-only   Only inject MCP config, skip the skill
      --dry-run       Preview changes without applying them
      --force         Overwrite existing agent profile and MCP config entries
  -h, --help          help for install
      --http          Use HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token

agent profile, updating all capability fields. The legacy alias "read-only"
is accepted as a synonym for "safe". Use --dry-run to preview changes without

help.symvault broker:
Run an opt-in loopback MITM forward proxy that attaches vault
credentials to the agent's outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests server-side.

A brokered secret never enters the agent's process environment, argv or
process listing: the child process only receives HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and
the path to the broker's CA certificate. Hosts covered by an API template
get credential injection; unmatched hosts are forwarded untouched (or
rejected with 403 in --strict mode). Hosts in --passthrough are tunneled
without TLS interception (escape hatch for certificate-pinning clients).

Same-machine limitation: on one host this removes the plaintext from the
child environment, but an agent with the user's own filesystem access can
still reach the vault. Deploy the broker on a separate host (or the agent
in a container) for the strong guarantee.

The broker exits on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The generated CA certificate is written
to <vault>/broker-ca.pem.

Usage:
  symvault broker [flags]

Examples:
  # Start the broker on an ephemeral loopback port
  symvault broker

  # Fixed port, strict mode (unmatched hosts get 403)
  symvault broker --addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --strict

  # Pass through hosts whose clients pin certificates
  symvault broker --passthrough corporate.internal,legacy.example.com

  # Use with a child process (env exports are printed at startup)
  symvault run --broker -- gh pr create

Flags:
      --addr string           Loopback listen address (0 selects an ephemeral port) (default "127.0.0.1:0")
  -h, --help                  help for broker
      --passthrough strings   Hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)
      --strict                Reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

help.symvault device join:
Join an existing vault from a remote git repository.

Clones the vault repository, reads the pairing token file to obtain
the existing device's public key, generates a new identity for this device,
and submits this device's public key back to the vault.

After completion, the existing device must run 'symvault device accept <token>'
to re-encrypt all entries for this new device.

To join without a git remote, pass the invitation artifact directly with
--pairing-file. The file is the <token>.json written by 'symvault device pair'
on the existing device; it can travel over any channel (synced folder, AirDrop,
manual copy). The response artifact is then left in the local vault directory
as <token>-response.json for delivery back to the existing device by any
means; 'symvault device accept' accepts both <token>-joined.json (git flow)
and <token>-response.json (file flow).

Usage:
  symvault device join <remote-url> <token> [flags]

Examples:
  symvault device join ssh://user@host/path/to/vault.git 123456
  symvault device join --pairing-file ~/Downloads/ABCD1234.json

Flags:

help.symvault import:
Imports password entries from another password manager.

When --format is not specified, the format is auto-detected from the input file extension:
  .csv  → CSV format
  .json → JSON format
  .yaml/.yml → YAML format
  .zip  → CXF format (FIDO Credential Exchange Format archive)

CSV files are additionally header-sniffed: exports from Apple Passwords
(iCloud Keychain), Chrome/Chromium and Firefox are recognized from their
header row and mapped with a built-in profile. Use --format apple, --format
chrome or --format firefox to select a profile explicitly. Use --format to
override auto-detection or when the file extension does not match the actual
format.

Usage:
  symvault import <source> [flags]
  symvault import [command]

Examples:
  # Auto-detect format from file extension
  symvault import bw-export.json --dry-run

  # Auto-detect the CSV profile from the header row (Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox)
  symvault import passwords.csv --dry-run

  # Import a FIDO Credential Exchange Format (CXF) archive (Apple Passwords, Bitwarden, Dashlane, ...)
  symvault import export.zip --format cxf --dry-run

  # Explicitly specify a format (overrides auto-detection)
  symvault import bitwarden bw-export.json --dry-run

  # Import a Firefox export under a prefix, skipping entries that already exist
  symvault import logins.csv --format firefox --prefix work/ --skip-existing

  # Auto-detect CSV from .csv extension
  symvault import data.csv --overwrite

help.symvault intake:
Validates loose credential material (text files, .env exports, JSON,
screenshots, certificate/key files, backup-code images) and stages it as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine/<import-id>/ for human review
before any agent can read it.

Sources are validated (regular files only, stable size/mtime, per-file and
batch limits), copied atomically into a private spool, content-sniffed (never
trusting extensions), and parsed into field/attachment suggestions. The
exact source bytes are stored as an encrypted attachment with SHA-256, size
and source-type provenance. Nothing is written to normal vault paths.

Promote a batch after review:
  symvault intake review promote <import-id>   (alias of import review promote)

Source files are never deleted unless --move-to-trash is given (macOS only)
and only after the quarantine entry was written and verified.

Usage:
  symvault intake <file...> [flags]
  symvault intake [command]

Examples:
  # Dry-run: validate, sniff and show suggestions without writing
  symvault intake ~/Downloads/creds.env ~/Downloads/backup.png --dry-run

  # Machine-readable dry-run (metadata only, never secret values)
  symvault intake ~/Downloads/token.json --dry-run --json

  # Stage a review batch and print the import id
  symvault intake ~/Downloads/elster.p12 ~/Downloads/recovery-codes.png

  # Promote the reviewed batch into normal vault paths
  symvault import review promote intake-20260827-1a2b3c4d

help.symvault intake watch:
Watches a user-selected folder for new credential material (screenshots,
exports, certificate files, backup codes) and stages each pickup as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine/<import-id>/. The watcher is
deliberately conservative:

- Files are only picked up after their size and mtime stabilized (debounce);
  partial downloads and files still being written are skipped.
- Sources are never deleted, never moved, and never auto-promoted. Review
  and promotion happen through `import review promote`.
- Already-staged files are remembered across polls (ledger), so the same
  file is not intaked twice.

Run with --once for a single scan (cron/LaunchAgent friendly). For an
always-on watcher, run without --once and stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or
SIGTERM; to pause, stop the process and restart it later. To disable, remove
the LaunchAgent entry or stop invoking the command.

Example LaunchAgent plist (adjust paths):
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.symaira.vault-intake.plist
  ProgramArguments: [ /usr/local/bin/symvault, intake, watch, /path/to/folder, --once ]
  StartInterval: 300

Usage:
  symvault intake watch <directory> [flags]
  symvault intake watch [command]

Examples:
  # One scan, stage anything new (cron-friendly)
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once

  # Machine-readable single scan
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once --json

  # Always-on watcher with a 15s poll interval
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --interval 15s

help.symvault migrate kdf:
Migrate the vault identity's key derivation function from the legacy
scrypt KDF to argon2id.

Argon2id is the industry standard for password hashing and provides stronger
resistance against GPU-based attacks than scrypt. New vaults already use
argon2id.

This command performs the migration itself — it does not just report status.
Automatic migration on every unlock additionally happens when
vault.auto_migrate_kdf: true is set in config.yaml, but by default that is
off, so this command is the way to upgrade an existing scrypt vault.

identity.age is backed up to identity.age.bak before any change, and the new
file is decrypt-verified before the migration is considered done. On any
failure the original identity.age is restored automatically. Changing
config.yaml's scrypt_work_factor alone does not perform this migration —
only this command (or auto_migrate_kdf) re-encrypts identity.age.

Older Argon2 budgets require --allow-legacy-kdf. This local migration retains
identity/config backups and rewrites the same identity with current defaults.

help.symvault run:
Executes a command with vault secrets injected as environment variables. Use --env NAME=path.field to map secrets.

With --broker the child's outbound traffic is routed through an in-process egress credential broker, so brokered secrets never enter the child environment. The broker mode is configured with --broker-strict (reject hosts without a matching template) and --broker-passthrough (tunnel certificate-pinning hosts without TLS interception).

Usage:
  symvault run [flags] -- <command> [args...]

Examples:
  # Inject AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from vault entry "work/aws.secret"
  symvault run --env AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=work/aws.secret -- aws s3 ls

  # Multiple secrets from env file
  symvault run --env-file .env.symvault -- npm run dev

  # Pass through parent NODE_ENV and PORT to the child process
  NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080 symvault run --passthrough NODE_ENV,PORT -- npm start

  # Route the child through the egress broker: strict mode, with one
  # certificate-pinning host tunneled without TLS interception
  symvault run --broker --broker-strict --broker-passthrough corp.internal -- ./deploy.sh

  # Multiple secrets, custom working dir
  symvault run \
    --env DB_PASS=prod/db.password \
    --env API_TOKEN=stripe.token \
    --workdir /tmp/job -- ./deploy.sh

Flags:
      --broker                       Route the child's outbound traffic through the egress credential broker (credentials never enter the child environment); configure with --broker-strict and --broker-passthrough
      --broker-passthrough strings   With --broker: hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)
      --broker-strict                With --broker: reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403
  -e, --env stringArray              Environment variable mapping (NAME=path.field)
  -f, --env-file stringArray         File with env variable mappings (NAME=path.field), one per line

      --passthrough stringArray      Parent env var names to pass through to the child process (comma-separated)

automatically select entries matching a vault path prefix. Each ref is a
vault entry path with an optional dot-separated field (e.g. db.password).

help.symvault verify:
Verify that all vault entries match their recorded manifest hashes.
This detects tampered or corrupted entry files.

Use --rebuild to regenerate the manifest from the on-disk .age files (use
this when entries have been added out-of-band, e.g. via git sync, and the
manifest has not been updated). Use --rebuild-only to skip the integrity
check and only rebuild.

Usage:
  symvault verify [flags]

Examples:
  # Verify manifest matches on-disk entries
  symvault verify

  # Rebuild the manifest from on-disk entries (fixes "unknown" entries from sync)
  symvault verify --rebuild

  # Just rebuild, skip the integrity check

    # bash focuses on the part after the =, so we need to remove
    # the flag part from $cur

    out=$(eval "${requestComp}" 2>/dev/null)

    directive=${out##*:}

    __symvault_debug "The completions are: ${out}"

__symvault_process_completion_results() {
    local shellCompDirectiveError=1
    local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=2
    local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=4
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=8
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=16
    local shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder=32

    if (((directive & shellCompDirectiveError) != 0)); then
        # Error code.  No completion.
        __symvault_debug "Received error from custom completion go code"
        return

                __symvault_debug "Activating no space"
                compopt -o nospace
            else
                __symvault_debug "No space directive not supported in this version of bash"
            fi
        fi

            if [[ $(type -t compopt) == builtin ]]; then

                if [[ ${BASH_VERSINFO[0]} -lt 4 || ( ${BASH_VERSINFO[0]} -eq 4 && ${BASH_VERSINFO[1]} -lt 4 ) ]]; then

            fi

            if [[ $(type -t compopt) == builtin ]]; then
                __symvault_debug "Activating no file completion"
                compopt +o default
            else
                __symvault_debug "No file completion directive not supported in this version of bash"
            fi
        fi
    fi

    local completions=()
    local activeHelp=()

        # File extension filtering
        local fullFilter="" filter filteringCmd

        for filter in ${completions[*]}; do

        else
            __symvault_debug "Listing directories in ."
            _filedir -d
        fi
    else
        __symvault_handle_completion_types
    fi

    __symvault_handle_special_char "$cur" =

    __symvault_handle_activeHelp

__symvault_handle_activeHelp() {
    # Print the activeHelp statements
    if ((${#activeHelp[*]} != 0)); then
        if [ -z $COMP_TYPE ]; then
            # Bash v3 does not set the COMP_TYPE variable.
            printf "\n";
            printf "%s\n" "${activeHelp[@]}"
            printf "\n"
            __symvault_reprint_commandLine
            return
        fi

        # Only print ActiveHelp on the second TAB press
        if [ $COMP_TYPE -eq 63 ]; then
            printf "\n"
            printf "%s\n" "${activeHelp[@]}"

            if ((${#COMPREPLY[*]} == 0)); then
                # When there are no completion choices from the program, file completion
                # may kick in if the program has not disabled it; in such a case, we want
                # to know if any files will match what the user typed, so that we know if
                # there will be completions presented, so that we know how to handle ActiveHelp.

                # the call to _filedir will fill COMPREPLY if files match.
                if (((directive & shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp) == 0)); then

                    _filedir
                fi

                # If there are completion choices to be shown, print a delimiter.
                # Re-printing the command-line will automatically be done
                # by the shell when it prints the completion choices.
                printf -- "--"
            else
                # When there are no completion choices at all, we need
                # to re-print the command-line since the shell will
                # not be doing it itself.
                __symvault_reprint_commandLine
            fi
        elif [ $COMP_TYPE -eq 37 ] || [ $COMP_TYPE -eq 42 ]; then
            # For completion type: menu-complete/menu-complete-backward and insert-completions
            # the completions are immediately inserted into the command-line, so we first
            # print the activeHelp message and reprint the command-line since the shell won't.
            printf "\n"
            printf "%s\n" "${activeHelp[@]}"

__symvault_reprint_commandLine() {
    # The prompt format is only available from bash 4.4.
    # We test if it is available before using it.
    if (x=${PS1@P}) 2> /dev/null; then
        printf "%s" "${PS1@P}${COMP_LINE[@]}"
    else

        # text the user had typed, it is workable enough.
        printf "%s" "${COMP_LINE[@]}"
    fi

# Separate activeHelp lines from real completions.
# Fills the $activeHelp and $completions arrays.
__symvault_extract_activeHelp() {
    local activeHelpMarker="_activeHelp_ "
    local endIndex=${#activeHelpMarker}

    while IFS='' read -r comp; do
        [[ -z $comp ]] && continue

        if [[ ${comp:0:endIndex} == $activeHelpMarker ]]; then
            comp=${comp:endIndex}
            __symvault_debug "ActiveHelp found: $comp"
            if [[ -n $comp ]]; then
                activeHelp+=("$comp")
            fi
        else
            # Not an activeHelp line but a normal completion
            completions+=("$comp")
        fi
    done <<<"${out}"
}

__symvault_handle_completion_types() {
    __symvault_debug "__symvault_handle_completion_types: COMP_TYPE is $COMP_TYPE"

    case $COMP_TYPE in
    37|42)
        # Type: menu-complete/menu-complete-backward and insert-completions
        # If the user requested inserting one completion at a time, or all
        # completions at once on the command-line we must remove the descriptions.
        # https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1508

        # If there are no completions, we don't need to do anything
        (( ${#completions[@]} == 0 )) && return 0

        local tab=$'\t'

        # Strip any description and escape the completion to handled special characters
        IFS=$'\n' read -ra completions -d '' < <(printf "%q\n" "${completions[@]%%$tab*}")

        # Only consider the completions that match
        IFS=$'\n' read -ra COMPREPLY -d '' < <(IFS=$'\n'; compgen -W "${completions[*]}" -- "${cur}")

        # compgen looses the escaping so we need to escape all completions again since they will
        # all be inserted on the command-line.
        IFS=$'\n' read -ra COMPREPLY -d '' < <(printf "%q\n" "${COMPREPLY[@]}")
        ;;

    *)
        # Type: complete (normal completion)
        __symvault_handle_standard_completion_case
        ;;
    esac
}

__symvault_handle_standard_completion_case() {
    local tab=$'\t'

    # If there are no completions, we don't need to do anything
    (( ${#completions[@]} == 0 )) && return 0

    # Short circuit to optimize if we don't have descriptions
    if [[ "${completions[*]}" != *$tab* ]]; then
        # First, escape the completions to handle special characters
        IFS=$'\n' read -ra completions -d '' < <(printf "%q\n" "${completions[@]}")
        # Only consider the completions that match what the user typed
        IFS=$'\n' read -ra COMPREPLY -d '' < <(IFS=$'\n'; compgen -W "${completions[*]}" -- "${cur}")

        # compgen looses the escaping so, if there is only a single completion, we need to
        # escape it again because it will be inserted on the command-line.  If there are multiple
        # completions, we don't want to escape them because they will be printed in a list
        # and we don't want to show escape characters in that list.
        if (( ${#COMPREPLY[@]} == 1 )); then
            COMPREPLY[0]=$(printf "%q" "${COMPREPLY[0]}")
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    local longest=0
    local compline
    # Look for the longest completion so that we can format things nicely
    while IFS='' read -r compline; do
        [[ -z $compline ]] && continue

        # Before checking if the completion matches what the user typed,
        # we need to strip any description and escape the completion to handle special
        # characters because those escape characters are part of what the user typed.
        # Don't call "printf" in a sub-shell because it will be much slower
        # since we are in a loop.
        printf -v comp "%q" "${compline%%$tab*}" &>/dev/null || comp=$(printf "%q" "${compline%%$tab*}")

        # Only consider the completions that match
        [[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue

        # The completions matches.  Add it to the list of full completions including
        # its description.  We don't escape the completion because it may get printed
        # in a list if there are more than one and we don't want show escape characters
        # in that list.
        COMPREPLY+=("$compline")

        # Strip any description before checking the length, and again, don't escape
        # the completion because this length is only used when printing the completions
        # in a list and we don't want show escape characters in that list.
        comp=${compline%%$tab*}
        if ((${#comp}>longest)); then
            longest=${#comp}
        fi
    done < <(printf "%s\n" "${completions[@]}")

    # If there is a single completion left, remove the description text and escape any special characters
    if ((${#COMPREPLY[*]} == 1)); then
        __symvault_debug "COMPREPLY[0]: ${COMPREPLY[0]}"
        COMPREPLY[0]=$(printf "%q" "${COMPREPLY[0]%%$tab*}")
        __symvault_debug "Removed description from single completion, which is now: ${COMPREPLY[0]}"
    else
        # Format the descriptions
        __symvault_format_comp_descriptions $longest
    fi
}

__symvault_handle_special_char()
{
    local comp="$1"
    local char=$2
    if [[ "$comp" == *${char}* && "$COMP_WORDBREAKS" == *${char}* ]]; then
        local word=${comp%"${comp##*${char}}"}
        local idx=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
        while ((--idx >= 0)); do
            COMPREPLY[idx]=${COMPREPLY[idx]#"$word"}
        done
    fi
}

__symvault_format_comp_descriptions()
{
    local tab=$'\t'
    local comp desc maxdesclength
    local longest=$1

    local i ci
    for ci in ${!COMPREPLY[*]}; do
        comp=${COMPREPLY[ci]}
        # Properly format the description string which follows a tab character if there is one
        if [[ "$comp" == *$tab* ]]; then
            __symvault_debug "Original comp: $comp"
            desc=${comp#*$tab}
            comp=${comp%%$tab*}

            # $COLUMNS stores the current shell width.
            # Remove an extra 4 because we add 2 spaces and 2 parentheses.
            maxdesclength=$(( COLUMNS - longest - 4 ))

            # Make sure we can fit a description of at least 8 characters
            # if we are to align the descriptions.
            if ((maxdesclength > 8)); then
                # Add the proper number of spaces to align the descriptions
                for ((i = ${#comp} ; i < longest ; i++)); do
                    comp+=" "
                done
            else
                # Don't pad the descriptions so we can fit more text after the completion
                maxdesclength=$(( COLUMNS - ${#comp} - 4 ))
            fi

            # If there is enough space for any description text,
            # truncate the descriptions that are too long for the shell width
            if ((maxdesclength > 0)); then
                if ((${#desc} > maxdesclength)); then
                    desc=${desc:0:$(( maxdesclength - 1 ))}
                    desc+="…"
                fi
                comp+="  ($desc)"
            fi
            COMPREPLY[ci]=$comp
            __symvault_debug "Final comp: $comp"
        fi
    done
}

__start_symvault()
{
    local cur prev words cword split

    COMPREPLY=()

    # Call _init_completion from the bash-completion package
    # to prepare the arguments properly
    if declare -F _init_completion >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _init_completion -n =: || return
    else
        __symvault_init_completion -n =: || return
    fi

    __symvault_debug
    __symvault_debug "========= starting completion logic =========="
    __symvault_debug "cur is ${cur}, words[*] is ${words[*]}, #words[@] is ${#words[@]}, cword is $cword"

    # The user could have moved the cursor backwards on the command-line.
    # We need to trigger completion from the $cword location, so we need
    # to truncate the command-line ($words) up to the $cword location.
    words=("${words[@]:0:$cword+1}")
    __symvault_debug "Truncated words[*]: ${words[*]},"

    local out directive
    __symvault_get_completion_results
    __symvault_process_completion_results
}

if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
    complete -o default -F __start_symvault symvault
else
    complete -o default -o nospace -F __start_symvault symvault
fi

__symvault_handle_standard_completion_case() {

    (( ${#completions[@]} == 0 )) && return 0

    if [[ "${completions[*]}" != *$tab* ]]; then

        # characters because those escape characters are part of what the user typed.
        # Don't call "printf" in a sub-shell because it will be much slower
        # since we are in a loop.
        printf -v comp "%q" "${compline%%$tab*}" &>/dev/null || comp=$(printf "%q" "${compline%%$tab*}")

        [[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue

        # its description.  We don't escape the completion because it may get printed
        # in a list if there are more than one and we don't want show escape characters
        # in that list.
        COMPREPLY+=("$compline")

        # Strip any description before checking the length, and again, don't escape
        # the completion because this length is only used when printing the completions
        # in a list and we don't want show escape characters in that list.
        comp=${compline%%$tab*}
        if ((${#comp}>longest)); then
            longest=${#comp}
        fi
    done < <(printf "%s\n" "${completions[@]}")

    # If there is a single completion left, remove the description text and escape any special characters
    if ((${#COMPREPLY[*]} == 1)); then
        __symvault_debug "COMPREPLY[0]: ${COMPREPLY[0]}"
        COMPREPLY[0]=$(printf "%q" "${COMPREPLY[0]%%$tab*}")
        __symvault_debug "Removed description from single completion, which is now: ${COMPREPLY[0]}"
    else
        # Format the descriptions
        __symvault_format_comp_descriptions $longest
    fi

__symvault_handle_special_char()
{
    local comp="$1"
    local char=$2
    if [[ "$comp" == *${char}* && "$COMP_WORDBREAKS" == *${char}* ]]; then
        local word=${comp%"${comp##*${char}}"}
        local idx=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
        while ((--idx >= 0)); do

        done

__symvault_format_comp_descriptions()
{

    local comp desc maxdesclength

    local i ci
    for ci in ${!COMPREPLY[*]}; do
        comp=${COMPREPLY[ci]}

        if [[ "$comp" == *$tab* ]]; then

            desc=${comp#*$tab}

function __symvault_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"

    end
end

function __symvault_perform_completion
    __symvault_debug "Starting __symvault_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __symvault_debug "args: $args"
    __symvault_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "SYMVAULT_ACTIVE_HELP=0 $args[1] __complete $args[2..-1] $lastArg"

    __symvault_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]
        if test (string trim -- $line) = ""
            # Found an empty line, remove it
            set results $results[1..-2]
        else
            # Found non-empty line, we have our proper output
            break
        end
    end

    set -l comps $results[1..-2]
    set -l directiveLine $results[-1]

    # For Fish, when completing a flag with an = (e.g., <program> -n=<TAB>)
    # completions must be prefixed with the flag
    set -l flagPrefix (string match -r -- '-.*=' "$lastArg")

    __symvault_debug "Comps: $comps"
    __symvault_debug "DirectiveLine: $directiveLine"
    __symvault_debug "flagPrefix: $flagPrefix"

function __symvault_perform_completion_once
    __symvault_debug "Starting __symvault_perform_completion_once"

    if test -n "$__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
        __symvault_debug "Seems like a valid result already exists, skipping __symvault_perform_completion"
        return 0
    end

    set --global __symvault_perform_completion_once_result (__symvault_perform_completion)
    if test -z "$__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
        __symvault_debug "No completions, probably due to a failure"
        return 1
    end

    __symvault_debug "Performed completions and set __symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
    return 0

    __symvault_debug ""

    __symvault_debug "Successfully erased the variable __symvault_perform_completion_once_result"

    __symvault_debug ""

    set --erase __symvault_comp_results

    __symvault_perform_completion_once
    __symvault_debug "Completion results: $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"

    if test -z "$__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
        __symvault_debug "No completion, probably due to a failure"
        # Might as well do file completion, in case it helps
        return 1
    end

    set -l directive (string sub --start 2 $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result[-1])
    set --global __symvault_comp_results $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result[1..-2]

    __symvault_debug "Completions are: $__symvault_comp_results"
    __symvault_debug "Directive is: $directive"

    set -l shellCompDirectiveError 1
    set -l shellCompDirectiveNoSpace 2
    set -l shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp 4
    set -l shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt 8
    set -l shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs 16

    if test -z "$directive"
        set directive 0
    end

    set -l compErr (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveError) % 2)
    if test $compErr -eq 1
        __symvault_debug "Received error directive: aborting."
        # Might as well do file completion, in case it helps
        return 1
    end

    set -l filefilter (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt) % 2)
    set -l dirfilter (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs) % 2)
    if test $filefilter -eq 1; or test $dirfilter -eq 1
        __symvault_debug "File extension filtering or directory filtering not supported"
        # Do full file completion instead
        return 1
    end

    set -l nospace (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveNoSpace) % 2)
    set -l nofiles (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp) % 2)

    __symvault_debug "nospace: $nospace, nofiles: $nofiles"

    # If we want to prevent a space, or if file completion is NOT disabled,
    # we need to count the number of valid completions.
    # To do so, we will filter on prefix as the completions we have received
    # may not already be filtered so as to allow fish to match on different
    # criteria than the prefix.
    if test $nospace -ne 0; or test $nofiles -eq 0
        set -l prefix (commandline -t | string escape --style=regex)
        __symvault_debug "prefix: $prefix"

        set -l completions (string match -r -- "^$prefix.*" $__symvault_comp_results)
        set --global __symvault_comp_results $completions
        __symvault_debug "Filtered completions are: $__symvault_comp_results"

        # Important not to quote the variable for count to work
        set -l numComps (count $__symvault_comp_results)
        __symvault_debug "numComps: $numComps"

        if test $numComps -eq 1; and test $nospace -ne 0
            # We must first split on \t to get rid of the descriptions to be
            # able to check what the actual completion will be.
            # We don't need descriptions anyway since there is only a single
            # real completion which the shell will expand immediately.
            set -l split (string split --max 1 \t $__symvault_comp_results[1])

            # Fish won't add a space if the completion ends with any
            # of the following characters: @=/:.,
            set -l lastChar (string sub -s -1 -- $split)
            if not string match -r -q "[@=/:.,]" -- "$lastChar"
                # In other cases, to support the "nospace" directive we trick the shell
                # by outputting an extra, longer completion.
                __symvault_debug "Adding second completion to perform nospace directive"
                set --global __symvault_comp_results $split[1] $split[1].
                __symvault_debug "Completions are now: $__symvault_comp_results"
            end
        end

        if test $numComps -eq 0; and test $nofiles -eq 0
            # To be consistent with bash and zsh, we only trigger file
            # completion when there are no other completions
            __symvault_debug "Requesting file completion"
            return 1
        end
    end

    return 0
end

# Since Fish completions are only loaded once the user triggers them, we trigger them ourselves
# so we can properly delete any completions provided by another script.
# Only do this if the program can be found, or else fish may print some errors; besides,
# the existing completions will only be loaded if the program can be found.
if type -q "symvault"
    # The space after the program name is essential to trigger completion for the program
    # and not completion of the program name itself.
    # Also, we use '> /dev/null 2>&1' since '&>' is not supported in older versions of fish.
    complete --do-complete "symvault " > /dev/null 2>&1
end

# Remove any pre-existing completions for the program since we will be handling all of them.
complete -c symvault -e

# this will get called after the two calls below and clear the $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result global
complete -c symvault -n '__symvault_clear_perform_completion_once_result'
# The call to __symvault_prepare_completions will setup __symvault_comp_results
# which provides the program's completion choices.
# If this doesn't require order preservation, we don't use the -k flag
complete -c symvault -n 'not __symvault_requires_order_preservation && __symvault_prepare_completions' -f -a '$__symvault_comp_results'
# otherwise we use the -k flag
complete -k -c symvault -n '__symvault_requires_order_preservation && __symvault_prepare_completions' -f -a '$__symvault_comp_results'

# fish completion for symvault                             -*- shell-script -*-

function __symvault_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"

    end
end

function __symvault_perform_completion
    __symvault_debug "Starting __symvault_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __symvault_debug "args: $args"
    __symvault_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "SYMVAULT_ACTIVE_HELP=0 $args[1] __completeNoDesc $args[2..-1] $lastArg"

    __symvault_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]
        if test (string trim -- $line) = ""
            # Found an empty line, remove it
            set results $results[1..-2]
        else
            # Found non-empty line, we have our proper output
            break
        end
    end

    set -l comps $results[1..-2]
    set -l directiveLine $results[-1]

    # For Fish, when completing a flag with an = (e.g., <program> -n=<TAB>)
    # completions must be prefixed with the flag
    set -l flagPrefix (string match -r -- '-.*=' "$lastArg")

    __symvault_debug "Comps: $comps"
    __symvault_debug "DirectiveLine: $directiveLine"
    __symvault_debug "flagPrefix: $flagPrefix"

    for comp in $comps
        printf "%s%s\n" "$flagPrefix" "$comp"
    end

    printf "%s\n" "$directiveLine"
end

# this function limits calls to __symvault_perform_completion, by caching the result behind $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result
function __symvault_perform_completion_once
    __symvault_debug "Starting __symvault_perform_completion_once"

        return 0
    end

    set --global __symvault_perform_completion_once_result (__symvault_perform_completion)
    if test -z "$__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
        __symvault_debug "No completions, probably due to a failure"
        return 1
    end

    __symvault_debug "Performed completions and set __symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
    return 0
end

# this function is used to clear the $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result variable after completions are run
function __symvault_clear_perform_completion_once_result
    __symvault_debug ""
    __symvault_debug "========= clearing previously set __symvault_perform_completion_once_result variable =========="
    set --erase __symvault_perform_completion_once_result
    __symvault_debug "Successfully erased the variable __symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
end

function __symvault_requires_order_preservation
    __symvault_debug ""
    __symvault_debug "========= checking if order preservation is required =========="

    __symvault_perform_completion_once
    if test -z "$__symvault_perform_completion_once_result"
        __symvault_debug "Error determining if order preservation is required"
        return 1
    end

    set -l directive (string sub --start 2 $__symvault_perform_completion_once_result[-1])
    __symvault_debug "Directive is: $directive"

    set -l shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder 32
    set -l keeporder (math (math --scale 0 $directive / $shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder) % 2)
    __symvault_debug "Keeporder is: $keeporder"

    if test $keeporder -ne 0

    end

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-add - Add a new password entry


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault add  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Creates a new password entry in the vault.

.PP
The entry name can use slash notation for organization (e.g., work/aws).
Interactive mode prompts for username, password, and URL.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--allow-empty\fP[=false]
	Allow empty value for sensitive fields

.PP
\fB--auto-rotate\fP[=false]
	Enable automatic rotation reminder

.PP
\fB--expires-at\fP=""
	Expiration date (RFC3339 format)

.PP
\fB--force\fP[=false]
	Skip password strength validation

.PP
\fB--generate\fP[=false]
	Generate a secure password (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for add

.PP
\fB--length\fP=20
	Generated password length for --generate

.PP
\fB--notes\fP=""
	Notes (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--stdin-totp-secret\fP[=false]
	Read TOTP secret from stdin (prevents argv leak)

.PP
\fB--stdin-value\fP[=false]
	Read password value from stdin (prevents argv leak)

.PP
\fB--totp-account\fP=""
	TOTP account name/username

.PP
\fB--totp-issuer\fP=""
	TOTP issuer/service name

.PP
\fB--totp-secret\fP=""
	TOTP secret key (base32 encoded, visible in process listings)

.PP
\fB--type\fP=""
	Secret type (api_key, bearer_token, basic_auth, ssh_key, password, certificate, database_url, totp_seed, custom). Auto-detected if not specified.

.PP
\fB--url\fP=""
	URL (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--usage-hint\fP=""
	Usage hint for AI agents

.PP
\fB--username\fP=""
	Username (non-interactive)

.PP
\fB--value\fP=""
	Password value (non-interactive, visible in process listings)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  symvault add github
  symvault add work/aws
  symvault add personal/bank
  symvault add github-token --value "my-secret-token"
  symvault add secure-pass --generate --length 20
  symvault add aws-key --type api_key --value "AKIA..."
  symvault add ssh-key --type ssh_key --usage-hint "Production server key"
.EE

\fBsymvault(1)\fP

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-agent-install - Install and configure an AI agent for Symaira Vault


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault agent install [name] [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Unified install command that detects an AI agent, creates a security
profile in config.yaml, generates a scoped access token, injects the
MCP server configuration into the agent's config file, and installs the
embedded skill package — all in one step.

.PP
This replaces the older mcp install, mcp-config, and agent setup commands.

.PP
The default security tier is "safe" (read-only capabilities). For "standard"
or "admin" tiers, an interactive terminal is required to confirm the
security implications.

.PP
Supported agents: openclaw, claude-code, hermes, codex, opencode


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--auto-detect\fP[=false]
	Detect all installed agents and configure each

.PP
\fB--config-only\fP[=false]
	Only inject MCP config, skip the skill

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Preview changes without applying them

.PP
\fB--force\fP[=false]
	Overwrite existing agent profile and MCP config entries

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for install

.PP
\fB--http\fP[=false]
	Use HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token

.PP
\fB--skill-only\fP[=false]
	Only install the skill package, skip MCP config

.PP
\fB--tier\fP="safe"
	Security tier: safe (default), standard, or admin


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Install and configure Claude Code (auto-detect)
  symvault agent install claude-code

  # Detect all installed agents and configure each
  symvault agent install --auto-detect

  # HTTP transport with auto-generated bearer token
  symvault agent install hermes --http

  # Standard tier with explicit confirmation
  symvault agent install codex --tier standard

  # Preview what would happen without writing anything
  symvault agent install openclaw --dry-run

  # Only install the skill package, skip MCP config
  symvault agent install opencode --skill-only

  # Only inject MCP config, skip the skill
  symvault agent install claude-code --config-only

  # Force overwrite existing profile and MCP config entries
  symvault agent install hermes --force

  # Structured JSON output for scripting
  symvault agent install opencode --output json
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault-agent(1)\fP

.SH NAME

.PP
The upgrade applies the named tier preset (safe, standard, or admin) to the
agent profile, updating all capability fields. The legacy alias "read-only"
is accepted as a synonym for "safe". Use --dry-run to preview changes without

an audit trail.

	help for upgrade

	Skip biometric verification (not recommended)

.PP

	Audit reason for the upgrade (required with --yes)

.PP
\fB--rotate-token\fP[=false]
	Rotate the agent's MCP token on upgrade

.PP
\fB--tier\fP=""
	Target security tier (safe, standard, admin; 'read-only' accepted as alias for 'safe')

.PP
\fB--yes\fP[=false]

.PP

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-agent-whoami - Show current agent context


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault agent whoami [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Display information about the current agent profile.

.PP
When the SYMVAULT_AGENT environment variable is set, loads that agent's profile
and shows name, tier, allowed paths, tools, quotas, and vault status.

.PP
The --output json flag returns structured data matching the MCP symaira_whoami
response format.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for whoami

.PP
\fB-o\fP, \fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Show agent context
  SYMVAULT_AGENT=my-agent symvault agent whoami

  # Show as JSON
  SYMVAULT_AGENT=my-agent symvault agent whoami --output json
.EE


.SH SEE ALSO
\fBsymvault-agent(1)\fP

.SH NAME
symvault-audit-export - Export audit evidence for auditor or incident-response bundles


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault audit export [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Export local audit evidence without exposing secret values.

.PP
Supports JSON and table output. Filter by time range, agent, and action.
Optionally verify HMAC integrity and redact vault paths.

	Agent name to filter by (default: all agents)

.PP

	Export only failed entries

.PP
\fB--format\fP="json"
	Output format: json or table

\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]

.PP
\fB--redact-paths\fP[=false]

.PP
\fB--since\fP=""
	Export entries since duration (e.g. 1h, 24h, 7d)

.PP
\fB--verify-hmac\fP[=false]
	Verify HMAC integrity of exported entries

.SH NAME
symvault-audit-rotate-key - Rotate the audit log HMAC key


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault audit rotate-key [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Generate a new HMAC key for audit log integrity and archive the current key.

.PP
The old key is archived to a file named after its fingerprint
(audit-hmac-key.rotated.) in the vault directory. A new audit
log file is started with the new key.

is archived and the command reports that it bootstrapped rather than

manpages.symvault-broker.1:
.nh
.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-broker - Run the egress credential broker (loopback MITM proxy)


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault broker [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Run an opt-in loopback MITM forward proxy that attaches vault
credentials to the agent's outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests server-side.

.PP
A brokered secret never enters the agent's process environment, argv or
process listing: the child process only receives HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and
the path to the broker's CA certificate. Hosts covered by an API template
get credential injection; unmatched hosts are forwarded untouched (or
rejected with 403 in --strict mode). Hosts in --passthrough are tunneled
without TLS interception (escape hatch for certificate-pinning clients).

.PP
Same-machine limitation: on one host this removes the plaintext from the
child environment, but an agent with the user's own filesystem access can
still reach the vault. Deploy the broker on a separate host (or the agent
in a container) for the strong guarantee.

.PP
The broker exits on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The generated CA certificate is written
to /broker-ca.pem.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--addr\fP="127.0.0.1:0"
	Loopback listen address (0 selects an ephemeral port)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for broker

.PP
\fB--passthrough\fP=[]
	Hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--strict\fP[=false]
	Reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS

.SH NAME
symvault-device-join - Join an existing vault as a new device


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault device join   [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Join an existing vault from a remote git repository.

.PP
Clones the vault repository, reads the pairing token file to obtain
the existing device's public key, generates a new identity for this device,
and submits this device's public key back to the vault.

.PP
After completion, the existing device must run 'symvault device accept \&'
to re-encrypt all entries for this new device.

.PP
To join without a git remote, pass the invitation artifact directly with
--pairing-file. The file is the \&.json written by 'symvault device pair'
on the existing device; it can travel over any channel (synced folder, AirDrop,
manual copy). The response artifact is then left in the local vault directory
as -response.json for delivery back to the existing device by any
means; 'symvault device accept' accepts both -joined.json (git flow)
and -response.json (file flow).

\fB--name\fP=""

.SH NAME
symvault-device-pair - Generate a pairing token for a new device


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault device pair [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Generate a pairing token that another device can use to join this vault.

.PP
This saves the pairing token and this device's public key to the vault,
commits and pushes the token file. The joining device reads this file
to obtain this device's public key for encryption.

.PP
IMPORTANT: After the joining device submits its public key (via 'symvault device join'),

	Output in JSON format (deprecated: use --output=json)

.SH NAME
symvault-import - Import entries from another password manager


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault import  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Imports password entries from another password manager.

.PP
When --format is not specified, the format is auto-detected from the input file extension:
  .csv  → CSV format
  .json → JSON format
  .yaml/.yml → YAML format
  .zip  → CXF format (FIDO Credential Exchange Format archive)

.PP
CSV files are additionally header-sniffed: exports from Apple Passwords
(iCloud Keychain), Chrome/Chromium and Firefox are recognized from their
header row and mapped with a built-in profile. Use --format apple, --format
chrome or --format firefox to select a profile explicitly. Use --format to
override auto-detection or when the file extension does not match the actual
format.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Parse import source without writing entries

.PP
\fB--format\fP=""
	Import format (auto-detected from file extension when omitted)

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for import

.PP
\fB--mapping\fP=""
	CSV column mapping (format: title=col1,username=col2,...)

.PP
\fB--overwrite\fP[=false]
	Delete existing entries before writing

.PP
\fB--prefix\fP=""
	Prepend path to all imported entries

.PP
\fB--quarantine\fP[=false]
	Import entries into quarantine// for human review before agent access

.PP
\fB--skip-existing\fP[=false]
	Skip entries that already exist


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Auto-detect format from file extension
  symvault import bw-export.json --dry-run

  # Auto-detect the CSV profile from the header row (Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox)
  symvault import passwords.csv --dry-run

  # Import a FIDO Credential Exchange Format (CXF) archive (Apple Passwords, Bitwarden, Dashlane, ...)
  symvault import export.zip --format cxf --dry-run

  # Explicitly specify a format (overrides auto-detection)
  symvault import bitwarden bw-export.json --dry-run

  # Import a Firefox export under a prefix, skipping entries that already exist
  symvault import logins.csv --format firefox --prefix work/ --skip-existing

  # Auto-detect CSV from .csv extension
  symvault import data.csv --overwrite

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-intake-watch - Watch a folder for new credential files and stage quarantined batches


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake watch  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Watches a user-selected folder for new credential material (screenshots,
exports, certificate files, backup codes) and stages each pickup as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine//. The watcher is
deliberately conservative:
.IP \(bu 2
Files are only picked up after their size and mtime stabilized (debounce);
partial downloads and files still being written are skipped.
.IP \(bu 2
Sources are never deleted, never moved, and never auto-promoted. Review
and promotion happen through \fBimport review promote\fR\&.
.IP \(bu 2
Already-staged files are remembered across polls (ledger), so the same
file is not intaked twice.

.PP
Run with --once for a single scan (cron/LaunchAgent friendly). For an
always-on watcher, run without --once and stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or
SIGTERM; to pause, stop the process and restart it later. To disable, remove
the LaunchAgent entry or stop invoking the command.

.PP
Example LaunchAgent plist (adjust paths):
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.symaira.vault-intake.plist
  ProgramArguments: [ /usr/local/bin/symvault, intake, watch, /path/to/folder, --once ]
  StartInterval: 300


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--debounce\fP=5s
	Require files to be stable for this long before pickup

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for watch

.PP
\fB--interval\fP=10s
	Poll interval (always-on mode)

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Emit machine-readable JSON per scan

.PP
\fB--once\fP[=false]
	Run a single scan and exit


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # One scan, stage anything new (cron-friendly)
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once

  # Machine-readable single scan
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --once --json

  # Always-on watcher with a 15s poll interval
  symvault intake watch ~/Downloads/intake --interval 15s
.EE

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-intake - Review-gated credential intake from loose files


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault intake  [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Validates loose credential material (text files, .env exports, JSON,
screenshots, certificate/key files, backup-code images) and stages it as a
quarantined review batch under quarantine// for human review
before any agent can read it.

.PP
Sources are validated (regular files only, stable size/mtime, per-file and
batch limits), copied atomically into a private spool, content-sniffed (never
trusting extensions), and parsed into field/attachment suggestions. The
exact source bytes are stored as an encrypted attachment with SHA-256, size
and source-type provenance. Nothing is written to normal vault paths.

.PP
Promote a batch after review:
  symvault intake review promote    (alias of import review promote)

.PP
Source files are never deleted unless --move-to-trash is given (macOS only)
and only after the quarantine entry was written and verified.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--batch-limit\fP=33554432
	Maximum total bytes per intake run

.PP
\fB--dry-run\fP[=false]
	Validate and report without writing anything

.PP
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for intake

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Emit machine-readable JSON (metadata only, never secret values)

.PP
\fB--max-files\fP=100
	Maximum number of files per intake run

.PP
\fB--move-to-trash\fP[=false]
	Move verified source files to the macOS Trash after the quarantine entry is written (macOS only)

.PP
\fB--ocr-text\fP=""
	Path to a text file with on-device OCR results; its lines become suggestions for image/PDF sources (macOS client integration)


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Dry-run: validate, sniff and show suggestions without writing
  symvault intake ~/Downloads/creds.env ~/Downloads/backup.png --dry-run

  # Machine-readable dry-run (metadata only, never secret values)
  symvault intake ~/Downloads/token.json --dry-run --json

  # Stage a review batch and print the import id

  # Promote the reviewed batch into normal vault paths

.SH NAME
symvault-migrate-kdf - Migrate the vault identity from scrypt to argon2id


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault migrate kdf [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Migrate the vault identity's key derivation function from the legacy
scrypt KDF to argon2id.

.PP
Argon2id is the industry standard for password hashing and provides stronger
resistance against GPU-based attacks than scrypt. New vaults already use
argon2id.

.PP
This command performs the migration itself — it does not just report status.
Automatic migration on every unlock additionally happens when
vault.auto_migrate_kdf: true is set in config.yaml, but by default that is
off, so this command is the way to upgrade an existing scrypt vault.

.PP
identity.age is backed up to identity.age.bak before any change, and the new
file is decrypt-verified before the migration is considered done. On any
failure the original identity.age is restored automatically. Changing
config.yaml's scrypt_work_factor alone does not perform this migration —
only this command (or auto_migrate_kdf) re-encrypts identity.age.

.PP
Older Argon2 budgets require --allow-legacy-kdf. This local migration retains
identity/config backups and rewrites the same identity with current defaults.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--allow-legacy-kdf\fP[=false]
	Allow one exclusive historical-budget read for local Argon2 policy migration

	help for kdf

.TH "SYMVAULT" "1" "Jan 1970" "Symaira Vault" "Symaira Vault Manual"

.SH NAME
symvault-run - Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault run [flags] --  [args...]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Executes a command with vault secrets injected as environment variables. Use --env NAME=path.field to map secrets.

.PP
With --broker the child's outbound traffic is routed through an in-process egress credential broker, so brokered secrets never enter the child environment. The broker mode is configured with --broker-strict (reject hosts without a matching template) and --broker-passthrough (tunnel certificate-pinning hosts without TLS interception).


.SH OPTIONS
\fB--broker\fP[=false]
	Route the child's outbound traffic through the egress credential broker (credentials never enter the child environment); configure with --broker-strict and --broker-passthrough

.PP
\fB--broker-passthrough\fP=[]
	With --broker: hosts tunneled without TLS interception (comma-separated, domain suffixes match)

.PP
\fB--broker-strict\fP[=false]
	With --broker: reject requests to hosts without a matching template with 403

.PP
\fB-e\fP, \fB--env\fP=[]
	Environment variable mapping (NAME=path.field)

.PP

.SH NAME
symvault-verify - Verify vault entry integrity against manifest


.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBsymvault verify [flags]\fP


.SH DESCRIPTION
Verify that all vault entries match their recorded manifest hashes.
This detects tampered or corrupted entry files.

.PP
Use --rebuild to regenerate the manifest from the on-disk .age files (use
this when entries have been added out-of-band, e.g. via git sync, and the
manifest has not been updated). Use --rebuild-only to skip the integrity
check and only rebuild.


.SH OPTIONS
\fB-h\fP, \fB--help\fP[=false]
	help for verify

.PP
\fB--rebuild\fP[=false]
	Rebuild the manifest from on-disk entries after the integrity check

.PP
\fB--rebuild-only\fP[=false]
	Rebuild the manifest and skip the integrity check


.SH OPTIONS INHERITED FROM PARENT COMMANDS
\fB--color\fP="auto"
	When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never

.PP
\fB--json\fP[=false]
	Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified

.PP
\fB--no-pipe-warning\fP[=false]
	suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets

.PP
\fB--output\fP="text"
	Output format (text, json, yaml)

.PP
\fB--profile\fP=""
	use a named vault profile

.PP
\fB--quiet\fP[=false]
	suppress non-error output

.PP
\fB--theme\fP=""
	Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)

.PP
\fB--vault\fP="~/.symvault"
	path to the password vault


.SH EXAMPLE
.EX
  # Verify manifest matches on-disk entries
  symvault verify

  # Rebuild the manifest from on-disk entries (fixes "unknown" entries from sync)
  symvault verify --rebuild

  # Just rebuild, skip the integrity check
  symvault verify --rebuild-only

  # As part of a scripted health check
  symvault verify || echo "Manifest mismatch — investigate"
.EE

.SH NAME

  symvault add       add a credential
